                                               1.0 SUMMARY

Cameron-Cole, LLC (Cameron-Cole) has completed a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) for an
approximately 7.82-acre property located at 669 Gilman Street and 1101, 1199, 1201, & 1203 Second
Street, Berkeley, Alameda County, California, hereinafter referred to as the “property”, “subject property”,
or “SP” (Figure 1). Although not referenced in the project address, our SP site reconnaissance and historical
records review additionally identified 1231 Second Street to be associated with the property at 1203 Second
Street. The scope of services generally conforms to the scope and limitations of the American Society for
Testing and Materials International (ASTM International) Standard Practice for Environmental Site
Assessments, Designation: E1527-21. The purpose of this Phase I ESA is to identify, to the extent feasible
pursuant to the ASTM International Standard E1527-21, recognized environmental conditions (RECs) in
connection with the subject property.

According to records maintained by the Alameda County Assessor’s Office and the City of Berkeley, the
subject property consists of twelve parcels or sections of parcels with assessor parcel numbers (APNs) 60-
2382-3-3, 60-2382-1-2, 60-2382-3-1, 60-2362-1-9, 60-2362-1-11, 60-2362-1-8, 60-2362-1-10, 60-2362-4-
2, 60-2382-6, 66-2686-20, 60-2362-2, and 60-2381-2-2 (Figure 2). The small north-most parcel APN 60-
2382-3-1, is identified by Alameda County Assessor’s Office as owned by Target while the remaining eleven
parcels are listed as owned by the City of Berkeley, California. A more detailed discussion of the parcels
associated with the subject property is provided in Section 4 of this ESA report.

The City operates the transfer facility, the large vehicle maintenance building, and administrative offices on
the subject property. The western one-fourth of the northern parcel (APN 60-2382-3-3) located at 1101
Second Street, is leased by Trillium Natural Gas, which operates is a natural gas compression, storage, and
commercial self-serve dispensing station. Ecology Center is a contractor to the City of Berkeley that operates
eight residential recycling routes and is located in the modular buildings at 1203 (alternatively 1231) Second
Street (APN 60-2362-1-8) immediately south of the administration offices. The far south portion of the subject
property, located at 669 Gilman Street (APN 60-2362-1-10), supports the Community Conservation Center,
a contractor to the City that collects, sorts, aggregates recyclable materials that are shipped to appropriate
material recyclers. Figure 3 shows existing conditions, service uses, and buildings on the subject property.

The goal of this Phase I ESA is to identify the presence or likely presence of hazardous substances or
petroleum products on the subject property under conditions that indicate an existing release, a past release,
or a material threat of a future release of any hazardous substances or petroleum products in, on or, at a
property. The findings of this report are summarized below and may include known or suspect RECs,
controlled RECs (CRECs), historical RECs (HRECs), or de minimis conditions identified during the
performance of this Phase I ESA.

Any exceptions to, or deletions from, ASTM International Standard E1527-21 are described in Section 2.4 of
this report. This assessment has revealed the following REC, CREC, HREC, business environmental risks
(BERS) or significant data gaps in connection with the subject property as summarized in Section 8.0:

HRECs

    •   Historic Industrial Site Use: Prior to the current use of the SP as the existing solid waste and
        transfer station, the site was used for various industrial operations. Based on Sanborn maps and
        areal images, parts of the SP have been used for industrial operations since 1901. Various uses




                                                      5
of the SP included the use and storage of hazardous chemicals and petroleum products. The
following findings are associated with these prior operations:
      o The HIST AST – CA database indicates the historical presence of above-ground storage
          tanks (ASTs) onsite.
      o The HIST UST – CA database lists two 4,000-gallon underground storage tanks (USTs)
          of unknown installation date containing regular motor vehicle fuel and a 1,000-gallon UST
          of unknown installation date containing diesel motor vehicle fuel associated with
          Clementina Ltd. 1101 – Second St. The exact location of these USTs is unknown;
          however, based on the address, they were likely associated with the northern portion of
          the subject property on the parcel identified by APN 60-2382-3-3.
      o At the existing solid waste transfer station 1101 Second Street, the LUST REG 2 – CA
          database lists a leaky UST site overseen by the Regional Water Quality Control Board
          (RWQCB). The site had a 350-gallon tank containing waste oil and two tanks of
          unknown size which contained gasoline and diesel, respectively, that were removed on
          8/1/1991. The two tanks referenced are likely associated with the HIST USTs cited
          above. Total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) (gas and diesel), benzene, toluene,
          xylenes, ethylbenzene, oil and grease, and heavy metals were present in soil and/or
          groundwater before cleanup. Soil remediation was completed in 1991 after the tanks
          were removed and three groundwater wells were installed and monitored for one year
          following removal. After remediation, all compounds were below maximum contaminant
          levels. The LUST case was closed in a letter dated May 20, 1997. The exact location of
          this UST is unknown; however, based on the address, they were likely associated with
          the northern portion of the subject property on the parcel identified by APN 60-2382-3-3..
      o At the Southern Pacific Transportation Company, the LUST REG 2 – CA and
          LUFT_ALAMEDA COUNTY- CA databases list a leaky UST site overseen by the
          Alameda County Local Oversight Program. The database lists the case as closed as of
          8/30/2000. The exact location of this UST is unknown.
      o The Sanborn Maps indicate the presence of former carbide ponds in the same location
          as the existing transfer station associated with the prior operations of Air Reduction Sales
          Company. During the site visit, Mr. Gregory Apa indicated that the existing transfer
          station building and surrounding hardscape surfaces are located in the general vicinity of
          the former carbide ponds. Mr. Apa based this as what appeared to be lime-treated soil
          were encountered during asphalt resurfacing activities conducted in November 2016.
          These carbide ponds could present residual contamination in soil.
It is the opinion of the environmental professional (EP) that historical industrial use of the SP
including, but not limited to, the former USTs, ASTs, and carbide ponds, are considered an
HREC. While there is not a suspicion of specific soil or groundwater contamination, the inherent
variability of sample results, the size of the SP, and the historic uses, de minimis residual soil
contamination cannot be ruled out. As such, the EP recommends that, prior to site
redevelopment, a soil management plan (SMP) be prepared to adequately outline the procedures
that will be followed to evaluate and remove potentially contaminated soil associated with
historical operations. At a minimum the SMP should contain a background, recommended field
screening and soil sampling techniques, proposed soil analytical methods, suspect soil
segregation procedures, management of identified contaminated soil, and documentation
protocol.

        underneath the SP, particularly the southern part of the SP. The EP considers the potential
        presence of VOCs in groundwater in the subsurface of the SP to be a REC. Potential for
        contaminated groundwater under the site also presents a VEC on the SP. Based on this
        designation and the intention of this Phase I ESA to evaluate the site for future development, the
        EP recommends sub-slab vapor sampling and/or soil gas sampling associated with plans for
        future closed structures on the site.

Business Environmental Risks (BERS):
Industrial operations associated with the current use of the subject property present a number of BERs.




                                                    8
    •   Truck Wash: The Phase I ESA completed in 2021 by Environmental Assessment Specialists
        identified a truck wash area with an oil water separator onsite. This area was noted during the site
        visit by Cameron-Cole personnel and is denoted in Figure 3. There is no evidence that any
        release has occurred associated with these operations and the oil water separator. The
        operation of this truck wash area is a BER because if the oil water separator were to fail or the
        concrete and asphalt surface was to have a penetration, there is potential for oil, grease, solvent,
        and petroleum products to be released to the environment.
    •   Vehicle Maintenance Building and Service Bays: The City of Berkeley operates large vehicle
        maintenance and repair facility with four service bays on the subject property adjacent to the
        transfer station, denoted in Figure 3. Various hazardous substances and petroleum products are
        associated with vehicle maintenance operations. No drains, sumps, in ground lifts, or other
        penetrations in the slab were noted in this area during the site inspection. The operations of this
        maintenance and repair facility presents a BER due the potential for release due to the use of
        hazardous substances and petroleum products.
    •   Hazardous Waste Collection: Though the existing transfer station does not accept hazardous
        waste, some hazardous waste is inadvertently present in wastes that are brought to the property.
        Typically, this hazardous waste is sorted and stored in a separate area before it is removed from
        the subject property. The storage of this hazardous waste on the SP represents a BER.
    •   Stormwater Collection System: A large sump area with fitted Baker Tank located north of the
        transfer station area on the subject property (denoted on Figure 3 with a blue X as “stormwater
        holding AST”). Stormwater that does not qualify to be discharged directly to the municipal
        stormwater system is stored and discharged to domestic sewer (EBMUD) through industrial use
        permit. The entire site is capped by concrete of asphalt surfaces and has a sophisticated
        stormwater collection system that is permitted through the state of California. Stormwater on the
        subject property likely comes into contact with wastes that are stored on the subject property
        during operations. The stormwater collection system presents a BER because if there is a leak or
        malfunction of the system there is a potential for a release of hazardous stormwater to the
        environment.

Although there is no evidence of a release associated with the BERs described listed above, operation of
these BERs may have resulted in de minimis soil contamination near these features. Prior to
development and subsurface excavation, a property-wide SMP (discussed previously for the HRECs)
should be completed.

This summary does not contain all the information that is found in the full report. The report should be
read in its entirety to obtain a more complete understanding of the information provided and to aid in
decisions made or actions taken based on this information.

                                           2.0 INTRODUCTION



2.1   Purpose

Cameron-Cole performed a Phase I ESA for an approximately 7.82-acre property located at 669 Gilman
Street and 1101, 1199, 1201, & 1203 (alternatively 1231) Second Street, Berkeley, Alameda County,
California in accordance with the Master Environmental Services Agreement between Cameron-Cole, LLC.
and First Carbon Solutions (the Client) on behalf of the City of Berkeley (the User). The assessment was
conducted in general conformance with the ASTM International Standard E1527-21 Standard Practice for
Environmental Site Assessments. This ESA was designed to identify, to the extent feasible, the presence or
likely presence of RECs in connection with the property.

The purpose of this Phase I ESA is to allow the “User” to benefit from one of the defenses referenced in
the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (CERCLA) liability: the
innocent landowner defense, the contiguous property owner defense, or bona fide prospective purchaser
defense. These defenses are collectively referred to as the “landowner liability protections,” or “LLPs”.
ASTM International Standard E1527-21 constitutes “all appropriate inquiry into the previous ownership and
uses of the property consistent with good commercial or customary practice” as defined at 42 U.S.C.
§9601(35)(B). Cameron-Cole considers FCS to be the Client and City of Berkeley to be the “User” of this
report.

The goal of this Phase I ESA is to identify RECs in connection with the subject property consistent with
ASTM International Standard E1527-21. A REC is defined as:

        1) the presence of hazardous substances or petroleum products in, on, or at the subject
        property due to a release to the environment; 2) the likely presence of hazardous
        substances or petroleum products in, on, or at the subject property due to a release or
        likely release to the environment; or 3) the presence of hazardous substances or petroleum
        products in, on, or at the subject property under conditions that pose a material threat of a
        future release to the environment.

2.2     Detailed Scope of Services

The scope of services consists of completing a Phase I ESA in general accordance with ASTM International
Standard E1527-21.

2.3     Significant Assumptions

Historical resources, personal interviews, and federal and state agency files regarding site operations and
past historical use have been considered when presenting Cameron-Cole’s findings and opinions. Cameron-
Cole considers all information provided by our environmental database subcontractor regarding regulatory
status of facilities to be current, accurate, and complete. Although Cameron-Cole made no independent
investigation as to the accuracy and completeness of other information derived from secondary sources,
Cameron-Cole assumes such information is reliable and representative of site conditions.




                                                     10
2.4     Limitations and Exceptions of Assessment

2.4.1   Site-Specific Limitations
Subsurface investigations were not conducted as part of this assessment.

2.4.2   Data Gaps
A data gap is a lack of, or inability to, obtain information required by ASTM International Standard E1527-21
despite good faith efforts to gather such information. Data gaps may result from incompleteness in any of
the activities required by ASTM International Standard E1527-21. According to the ASTM International
Standard Practice E1527-21, data gaps are only significant if “other information and/or professional
experience raise reasonable concerns involving the data gap”. Cameron-Cole was unable to acquire
documents pertaining to historic releases on the site from the County of Alameda. In the opinion of
Cameron-Cole, several significant data gaps were encountered during the completion of this Phase I ESA.

2.4.3   General Limitations and Exceptions
The Phase I ESA is produced in accordance with customary principles and practices in the applicable fields
of environmental science and engineering. Cameron-Cole is not responsible for conclusions, opinions, or
recommendations made by others based upon the information presented herein.

Although industry standard practices are employed, Phase I ESAs are inherently limited, given that findings
and conclusions are developed from limited site evaluation and research. In performing a Phase I ESA,
Cameron-Cole can only rely upon those records regarding the subject property and surrounding properties
which are available to the public and which can reasonably be obtained by Cameron-Cole. Cameron-Cole's
opinions, conclusions and recommendations are therefore limited to those which can be derived from such
available and reasonably obtainable records. It is often necessary for Cameron-Cole to rely on information
prepared or obtained by others to complete the Phase I ESA. Cameron-Cole makes no warranty or
representation as to the accuracy or completeness of information obtained from third parties. Additionally,
changes may result with the passage of time with respect to characteristics of the subject property and
those of surrounding properties. Cameron-Cole and its representatives do not warrant for or against future
changes in operations or conditions, nor do they warrant for or against conditions present of a type or at a
location not specifically addressed in the Phase I ESA.

Subject to the limitations stated herein, the opinions presented in Phase I ESA are valid for a period
of 180 days from the date of issuance.

Air, soil, and groundwater testing are not part of the Phase I ESA. This Phase I ESA is not intended to
establish whether air, soil, or groundwater contamination, or waste disposal is present or not present on
the subject property or on surrounding properties. Knowledge of actual environmental conditions on the
subject property or on any surrounding properties can only be obtained from air, soil, and groundwater
testing, the installation of groundwater monitoring wells, and possible additional testing, all of which are
outside the scope of the Phase I ESA.

Reasonable efforts were made within the scope of the Phase I ESA to identify the presence of USTs, ASTs,
and ancillary equipment on or near the subject property. Limitations to the Phase I ESA exist regarding USTs
and ASTs, in as much as information was obtained by Cameron-Cole solely through its review of unobstructed
and readily accessible areas, database information, and interviews. Such methods (which are considered


                                                     11
industry standard) do not preclude the actual presence of subsurface equipment (including USTs) or regulated
materials that are hidden from view due to historical activity such as site paving, re-grading, construction, or
debris pile storage. Similarly, it is possible that additional UST facilities not listed in regulatory database files
may exist at the subject property or on properties adjacent to the subject property due to owner/operator
registration negligence, filing errors with the state regulatory agency or for other reasons over which Cameron-
Cole has no control or ability to determine.

Conclusions in the Phase I ESA regarding potential environmental impact of properties and facilities
surrounding the subject property are based upon reasonably available information obtained from
environmental databases and inferred groundwater flow direction.

No environmental assessment can wholly eliminate uncertainty regarding the potential for RECs in connection
with a property. Performance of a Phase I ESA is solely intended to reduce, but not eliminate, uncertainty
regarding the potential for RECs in connection with the subject property, and this practice recognizes
reasonable limits of time and cost. The Phase I ESA has been prepared for the exclusive use and benefit of
FCS subject to the terms and conditions specified in the Master Environmental Services Agreement between
Cameron-Cole, LLC. and FCS. The Phase I ESA is for the sole and exclusive use and benefit of FCS, our
Client. Cameron-Cole makes no warranty as to the Phase I ESA except as to FCS’s exclusive use of the
Phase I ESA. The Client bears the sole responsibility for ensuring that the Phase I ESA is distributed or
disseminated to only those third parties to whom FCS is strictly obligated by contract, law, regulation, or
ordinance to provide it. Cameron-Cole disclaims any and all liability to any person or entity other than FCS
who uses or relies on the Phase I ESA in any way whatsoever without the express written consent of both
FCS and Cameron-Cole.

Third-party reliance letters may be issued upon request and upon payment of the then current fee for such
letters, and only if Cameron-Cole, FCS, and the User provide express written consent for any such reliance
letters.




                                                         12
                                           3.0 SITE DESCRIPTION

3.1       Location and Legal Description

The subject property is located at 669 Gilman Street and 1101, 1199, 1201, & 1203 (alternatively 1231)
Second Street, Berkeley, Alameda County, California. A Site Location Map is provided as Figure 1.
According to records maintained by the Alameda County Assessor’s office and the City of Berkeley, the
subject property consists of twelve parcels or sections of parcels with APNs 60-2382-3-3, 60-2382-1-2, 60-
2382-3-1, 60-2362-1-9, 60-2362-1-11, 60-2362-1-8, and 60-2362-1-10, 60-2362-4-2, 60-2382-6, 66-2686-
20, 60-2362-2, and 60-2381-2-2. Figure 2 shows address and parcels of the subject property.

3.2       Site and Vicinity Characteristics

The subject property consists of multiple parcels with surface area totaling 7.82 acres, see Figure 2. The
subject property is in a predominantly industrial area, bound by Codornices Creek to the north, a Union
Pacific Railroad (UPRR) alignment to the east, Gillman Street to the south and Second Street to the west.

3.3       Current Uses of the Property

The current uses of the subject property are accounted for from north to south. Figure 3 shows existing
conditions, service uses, and buildings on the subject property.

1101 Second St – Trillium Natural Gas Filling Station (leased from City of Berkeley).

1201 Second St – City of Berkeley operates the existing transfer station. This facility processes 140,000
tons of municipal waste per year. This location also supports a City-Operated large vehicle maintenance
building (four repair bays).

1203 (alternatively 1231) Second St – The Ecology Center is a contractor-run operation that has 8 city
routes that collect 8,400 tons/yr of recyclables from residential communities. The collected materials are
processed by the Berkeley Recycling facility.

669 Gilman St – Contractor operated (Community Conservation Inc.) sorts, crush, and bale 15,000 tons/yr
of recyclables.

3.4       Descriptions of Structures, Roads, and Other Improvements to the Site

The property can be accessed via paved driveways along Gilman and Second Streets. The entirety of the
subject property is covered with building roof cover or paved/ concrete surfaces except for the southern
portion of the riparian corridor of Codornices Creek (Figure 3). Existing features onsite are shown in Figure
3. The following buildings were noted onsite:

      -   Three large open-air corrugated sheet-metal steel frame buildings with concrete slabs (Transfer
          Station and Tipping Floor building, glass recycling warehouse [Sort Platform], and paper recycling
          warehouse building [MRF – PAPER Sorting and Bailing]).

5.2.1      Database Descriptions

RCRA_TSDF: Resource Conservation and Recovery Act hazardous waste transportation storage
disposal and treatment facilities

AST – CA: Listing of tank facilities that are subject to the California Aboveground Petroleum Storage
Act

HIST AST – CA: Historical listing of tank facilities that are subject to the California Aboveground
Petroleum Storage Act

FID UST – CA: The State Water Resource Control Board’s Facility Inventory Database underground
storage tank locations listings

HIST UST – CA: Historical listings of underground storage tank facilities

UST – CA: Listing of active underground storage tank facilities

UST_ALAMEDA COUNTY – CA: Alameda County underground storage tank sites

CERCLIS NFRAP: The Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability
Information System (CERCLIS) provides a list of sites with No Further Remedial Action Planned from
the CERCLIS program database.

FEDERAL FACILITY: Sites where Federal Facilities Restoration and Reuse Office (FFRRO) arranged
cleanup for Base Closure and Property Transfer at Federal Facilities

CORRACTS: List of facilities where Resource Conservation and Recovery Act Corrective Action
Program used to investigate and remediate hazardous releases

LUFT_ALAMEDA COUNTY – CA: Listing of Alameda County leaking underground fuel tank sites


                                                       20
LUST REG 2 – CA: Leaking underground storage tanks in Region 2: Alameda, Contra Costa, San
Francisco, Santa Clara (north of Morgan Hill), San Mateo, Marin, Sonoma, Napa, and Solano counties

SLIC REG 2 – CA: List of Region 2 sites from GeoTracker Site Cleanup Program (formerly known as
SLIC) database

SLIC ALAMEDA COUNTY – CA: Listing of spills leaks investigation & cleanup sites in Alameda County

RCRA_ LQG, RCRA_NONGEN, RCRA_SQG, RCRA_VSQG: Resource Conservation and Recovery
Act listing of licensed large quantity generators (LQG), non-generators (NONGEN), small quantity
generators (SQG), and very small quantity generators (VSQG)

ENVIROSTOR – CA: Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) sites

SWF/LF – CA: Solid Waste Information System’s facility listing of solid waste facilities and landfills

HWG – CA: Hazardous waste generator listings

SWRCY – CA: Listing of facilities which perform recycled material processing activities

5.2.2   Subject Property Database Findings

The subject property was identified in the AST – CA, FID UST – CA, HIST AST – CA, HIST UST – CA, UST
– CA, UST_ALAMEDA COUNTY- CA, RCRA_LQG, RCRA_NONGEN, RCRA_SQG, LUST REG 2 – CA,
SLIC ALAMEDA COUNTY – CA, HWG – CA, SWF/LF – CA, and SWRCY – CA databases. Seven
addresses are associated with these database listings: 1201 Second St, 1231 Second St, 1101 Second St,
1075 Second St, 1235 Second St, 699 Gillman St, and Second St 947.

The AST – CA database lists the “existing transfer station” – 1201 Second Street and indicates the
presence of aboveground petroleum tanks onsite last inspected in 2021.

The FID UST – CA database lists the “existing transfer station” – 1201 Second Street. A UST with an
installation date of 11/01/1982 was listed in this database.

The HIST AST – CA database lists the “existing transfer station” – 1201 Second Street. The database has
no information of the size or contents of ASTs.

The HIST UST – CA database lists “Clementina Ltd.” – 1101 Second St. This address was listed on State
Water Resources Control Board paperwork with three USTs: two 4,000-gallon USTs of unknown installation
date containing regular motor vehicle fuel and a 1,000-gallon UST of unknown installation date containing
diesel motor vehicle fuel.

The UST – CA database lists the “existing transfer station” – 1201 Second St. The database lists two
10,000 gallon single-walled diesel USTs installed on 11/1/1982.

The UST_ALAMEDA COUNTY – CA database lists the “existing transfer station” – 1201 Second Street.
The USTs are listed as being permitted by the City of Berkeley Toxics Management Division and the City
of Berkeley.

The RCRA_LQG database lists the “existing transfer station” – 1199 Second Street. The database lists
this site as a large quantity generator with a start date of 1/1/1981. Wastes associated with this site are as
follows: off-specification, aged or surplus inorganics; other inorganic solid waste; latex waste; off-

                                                     21
specification, aged or surplus organics; other organic solids; empty containers; ignitable waste; corrosive
waste; and reactive waste. All violations listed on this database have been resolved.

The RCRA_NONGEN database lists the “Ecology Center” – 1231 Second St. No violations are listed on
this database.

The RCRA_SQG database lists “Ohio Medical Products” – 1231 Second Street. The database lists this
site as a small quantity generator. This database lists no violations.

The LUST REG 2 – CA database lists the “existing transfer station” – 1101 Second St and the “Southern
Pacific Transportation Company” – 1075 Second Street. At the “existing transfer station”, the database
lists a leaky UST site overseen by the RWQCB. The site had a 350-gallon tank containing waste oil and
two tanks of unknown size which contained gasoline and diesel, respectively, that were removed on
8/1/1991. TPH (gas and diesel), benzene, toluene, xylenes, ethylbenzene, oil and grease, and heavy metals
were present in soil and/or groundwater before cleanup. Soil remediation was completed in 1991 after the
tanks were removed and three groundwater wells were installed and monitored for one year following
removal. After remediation, all compounds were below maximum contaminant levels. The LUST case was
closed in a letter dated May 20, 1997. At the “Southern Pacific Transportation Company”, which was
previous company on the subject property, the databases list a leaky UST site overseen by the Alameda
County Local Oversight Program. The database lists the case as closed as of 8/30/2000. The “Southern
Pacific Transportation Company” was also listed in the LUFT_ALAMEDA COUNTY – CA database. The
specific locations of these cited database references are unknown; however, based on their addresses,
these would likely have been associated with the northern parcel identified by APN 60-2382-3-3.

The SLIC ALAMEDA COUNTY – CA database lists “Southern Pacific Transportation Com.” – 1075 Second
St. Alcan Ingot & Powder – 1069 Second Street formerly leased land from the Southern Pacific
Transportation Company. Alcon Ingot & Powder was generally located where the existing Trillium Natural
Gas Filling Station is located (a portion of APN 60-2382-3-3). Alcon Ingot & Powder listed as a Hazardous
Waste Facility in Envirostor. In 1982, during redevelopment activities, a UST, associated with Alcan Ingot
& Powder operations, was removed and it was discovered that this UST had been discharging mineral
spirits to the soil. Additionally, diesel fuel and other hydrocarbons were discovered in the Union Pacific
railroad (UPRR) alignment area immediately upgradient (to the east) of the SP. Affected soil from both
areas were removed and the groundwater was sampled. The mineral spirits area showed no groundwater
contamination and TPH was at levels below cleanup levels. The diesel hydrocarbon area showed low
levels of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX) compounds in the soil and groundwater and
residual hydrocarbons. Hydrocarbons were determined to not pose a significant risk according to the
DTSC. The RWQCB approved a remediation measure to prevent COCs from migrating back to subject
property, which is downgradient from the former contaminated soil. A geotextile fabric was laid on the
excavation where the contaminated soil had been removed followed with two feet of drain dock and a
second layer of geotextile fabric. Plastic sheeting was placed on the west wall of the excavation. In 1998,
the RWQCB concurred that the site met cleanup requirements. In 1999, the DTSC concluded no further
action.

The HWG – CA database lists numerous addresses and properties listed as “inactive” and one site listed
as “active”. The active site is the “existing transfer station” – 1199 Second Street.

5.2.1     Database Descriptions

ECHO (EPA Enforcement and Compliance History Online): Database that lists facilities in a community
to assess their compliance with environmental regulations

ICIS: Lists federal judicial enforcement information

STORMWATER: Listing of permitted stormwater sites.

CALEPA SITES – CA: Listing of California Environmental Protection Agency Regulated Sites from the
Certified Unified Program Agencies (CUPA).

CIWQS – CA and CIWQS 2 – CA (California Integrated Water Quality System): List facilities which
includes owner information, violations, inspections, and other regulatory matters.

HAZNET – CA: Listing of hazardous waste manifests from when hazardous waste is transported from
generators to permitted recycling treatment storage or disposal facilities by registered hazardous waste
transporters.

NPDES – CA: List sites that have National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits

RFR – CA: Lists State Water Resource Control Board regulated facilities

                                                   30
5.3     Vapor Encroachment Condition Summary

Cameron-Cole conducted a review of available environmental records and conditions observed on the subject
property and adjoining parcels to evaluate the potential for a VEC to exist on the subject property. Cameron-
Cole identified the potential presence of contaminated groundwater onsite due to plumes associated with the
following adjacent properties: 707 Park and 707 Gilman Street. These properties are both labeled on Figure
3 with yellow Xs. Based on the inferred groundwater gradient (to the west), depth to groundwater, and
physical setting information, the potential for a VEC to exist on the subject property cannot be ruled out.
Further justification for the designation of this VEC can be found in Section 8.0.

5.4     Unmappable Sites

The Envirosite Report includes a summary of sites that may be in the general area of the subject property
yet do not have adequate location addresses or latitude/longitude coordinates to pinpoint their location in
relation to the subject property. Three listings for the unmappable sites were identified. These unmappable
sites were not observed in the vicinity of the subject property during the site reconnaissance and are not
discussed further.

5.5     Additional Environmental Record Sources

In accordance with ASTM International E1527-21, 8.3.1, the objective of compiling and analyzing historical
property information and developing a history of the previous uses of the subject property, adjoining
properties, and surrounding area is to help identify the likelihood of past uses having led to recognized
environmental conditions in connection with the subject property. All obvious uses of the subject property
must be identified from the present, back to the subject property’s first developed use, or back to 1940,
whichever is earlier. The report must describe all identified uses, justify the earliest date identified for the
subject property’s first developed use, and explain the reason for any gaps in the history of use. This task
requires reviewing as many of the standard historical resources in ASTM International E1527-21, 8.3.4.1
through 8.3.4.8 as are necessary and both reasonably ascertainable and likely to be useful. Data failure occurs
when all the standard historical sources that are reasonably ascertainable and likely to be useful have been
reviewed and yet the objective has not been met. Data failure is not uncommon in trying to identify historical
uses at 5-year intervals back to first use or 1940 (whichever is earlier). If the data failure represents a
significant data gap to the EP, ASTM International Standard E1527-21 requires documentation of the impact
of the data gap on the ability of the EP to identify RECs. No significant historical use information data gaps
were encountered.

5.6     Physical Setting Sources

5.6.1   Topography
Figure 1 is a Site Location Map which includes information from the 2021 USGS 7.5 Minute Series, Richmond
quadrangle. The map was reviewed to establish the physical setting of the subject property and surrounding
area. The site lies approximately 15 ft above mean sea level and slopes gently to the west.

5.6.2   Soils/Geology
The Envirosite report provides a summary of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Soil Survey
of the subject property’s general area. According to the Envirosite Report, the primary soil components on-
site are identified as Urban land, Miscellaneous area. This type of classification has no information on soil
drainage or corrosion potential.

5.6.3   Hydrology
Based on topographic maps, and considering regional flow patterns, the groundwater flow in the vicinity of
the site is inferred to be in a southwesterly direction. Groundwater flow direction can be influenced by factors
such as surface topography, underground structures, seasonal fluctuation, soil and bedrock geology, and
production wells which were not considered in this interpretation.

                                       6.0 SITE RECONNAISSANCE

6.1       Methodology and Limiting Conditions

The methodology used by the Cameron-Cole representative during the October 13, 2022 site
reconnaissance consisted of visual observations of readily accessible areas of the subject property to
determine the presence or absence of hazardous substance or petroleum product storage areas or spills
as indicated by stressed vegetation, soil staining, storage tanks, drums, etc.

6.2       General Site Setting

The site is approximately 7.82 acres, according to the Alameda County Assessor’s office and the City of
Berkeley and consists of twelve parcels or sections of parcels with APNs 60-2382-3-3, 60-2382-1-2, 60-
2382-3-1, 60-2362-1-9, 60-2362-1-11, 60-2362-1-8, and 60-2362-1-10, 60-2362-4-2, 60-2382-6, 66-2686-
20, 60-2362-2, and 60-2381-2-2. The current uses of the subject property are accounted for from north to
south. Please see Figure 3 for additional detail.

1101 Second St – Trillium Natural Gas Filling Station (leased from City of Berkeley).

1201 Second St – City of Berkeley operates the existing transfer station. This facility processes 140,000
tons of municipal waste per year. This location also supports a City-Operated large vehicle maintenance
building (four repair bays).

1203 (alternatively 1231) Second St – The Ecology Center is a contractor-run operation that has 8 city
routes that collect 8,400 tons/yr of recyclables from residential communities. The collected materials are
processed by the Berkeley Recycling facility.

669 Gilman St – Contractor operated (Community Conservation Inc.) sorts, crush, and bale 15,000 tons/yr
of recyclables.

6.2.1     Geologic, Hydrogeologic, and Topographic Conditions
Based on topographic maps, and considering regional flow patterns, the groundwater flow in the vicinity of
the site is inferred to be in a westerly direction. Groundwater flow direction can be influenced by factors such
as surface topography, underground structures, seasonal fluctuation, soil and bedrock geology, and
production wells which were not considered in this interpretation.

6.2.2     General Description of Structures
Existing features onsite are shown in Figure 3. The following buildings were noted onsite:

      -   Three large open-air corrugated sheet-metal steel frame buildings with concrete slabs (Transfer
          Station and Tipping Floor building, glass recycling warehouse [Sort Platform], and paper recycling
          warehouse building [MRF – PAPER Sorting and Bailing]).

      -   Corrugated metal steel frame pole barn (Storage/Bin Repair) in northeast most corner of site with
          concrete slab foundation.

      -   Vehicle maintenance building for large equipment/vehicle repair with concrete slab with steel frame
          and sheet metal construction.

      -   Administration building (Admin Building 1/Container Shop/Offices) of concrete slab masonry and



                                                      43
          wood construction with an eastern annex (Canopy Area) that is steel frame with sheet metal walls.

      -   Smaller support structures are present throughout including a temporary modular building used by
          Ecology Center as an administrative office (Ecology Center Administrative Office), a
          Communications Room (located between the Canopy Area and the 90-Gallon Diesel AST [Figure
          3]), the Scale House, and numerous smaller sheds and shipping containers used as temporary
          storage of sorted waste materials that are accumulated and sent to various recyclers throughout
          the property.

6.2.3     Roads
Second Street is to west of the subject property, Gillman Street is to the south, and the UPRR alignment is
to east (gravel/ballast). There are no roads adjacent to the SP to the north.

6.2.4     Potable Water Supply
The subject property is provided potable water service by the East Bay Municipal Utility District (EBMUD).
6.2.5     Sewage Disposal System
The subject property is provided municipal sewer service by the EBMUD. No septic systems or cisterns were
located on the subject property.

Hazardous substances and petroleum products in connection with identified uses were not observed on
the subject property during the October 13, 2022, site reconnaissance.

with drywall, carpeted floors, and drop in ceilings. The interiors of the Transfer Station and Tipping Floor

The enclosed buildings on the subject property are heated and cooled by a combination of natural gas
and/or electricity. There was no visual observation that heating oil is used on the subject property as a
means of heating interior occupiable spaces. The remainder of the on-property buildings are open air with
no apparent heating or cooling attributes.

6.4.2   Stains or Corrosion
No stains or corrosion were observed during the site reconnaissance.

6.4.3   Drains and Sumps
Drain or sumps were not observed during the site reconnaissance.

6.5     Exterior Observations

6.5.1   Pits, Ponds, or Lagoons
Pits, ponds, and/or lagoons were not observed on the subject property by Cameron-Cole during the site
reconnaissance. A large sump area with fitted Baker Tank is located on the upper northern third of the Transfer
Station and Tippling Floor Building area. This feature is labeled as “Stormwater Holding AST” in Figure 3.
Stormwater that does not qualify to be discharged directly to the municipal stormwater system is stored and
discharged to domestic sewer (EBMUD) through an industrial use permit. The entire site has a sophisticated
stormwater collection system that is permitted through the state of California.

6.5.2   Stained Soil or Pavement
Motor oil stains were observed during the site reconnaissance across the site as a result of customer vehicle


                                                      45
leaks and heavy equipment. No gross surface staining was observed at the SP. Based on the impervious
surfaces, the observed stains are considered de minimis.

6.5.3   Stressed Vegetation
Stressed vegetation was not observed during the site reconnaissance.

6.5.4   Solid Waste
Given the existing use of the subject property as an existing solid waste transfer station, solid waste was
observed on-site. Additionally, the southern portion of the site (See Figure 3) supports the Ecology Center and
Community Conservation Inc., two contractors who manage recyclable materials which are sorted, stored, and
bundled for shipment to various off-site recycling facilities.

6.5.5   Wastewater
Cameron-Cole did not observe any wastewater on site.

6.5.6   Wells
Two groundwater monitoring wells related to the upgradient VOC investigation described above were
observed on the southeast portion of the subject property located in an alley just east of the Materials
Recovery Facility and are attributed to the ongoing investigation of the Terminal facility at 707 Gilman Street
(see Figure 3).

6.5.7   Septic Systems
Septic systems were not observed at the time of site reconnaissance.

records regarding environmental violations, releases, or hazardous material or petroleum product storage,
storage tanks, or other environmental concerns associated with the subject property and a reported state
hazardous waste database listing associated with the subject property. On November 17, 2022, in response to
the FOIA records request, the City of Berkeley Toxics Management Division provided a number of records to
Cameron-Cole regarding four addresses associated with the subject property: 669 Gilman, 1101 Second Street,
1199 Second Street, and 1203 Second Street. These records were reviewed by Cameron-Cole. These records
included forms for inspections of the stormwater system and site USTs. Violations were noted regarding these
inspections. Violations were mostly administrative or preventative in nature. Records associated with the two
10,000-gallon USTs (see Figure 3) currently on the subject property indicate former violations. Though none of
these violations indicate a release occurred onsite, a number of them indicate that past leak detection might have
been insufficient to detect potential leaks. This additional information supports our opinion that the presence of
the single-walled 10,000-gallon USTs on the subject property represents a REC and that the stormwater
management system presents a BER.

                                                       47
                                    8.0 FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS

The goal of this Phase I ESA is to identify the presence or likely presence of hazardous substances or
petroleum products on the subject property under conditions that indicate an existing release, a past release,
or a material threat of release of any hazardous substances or petroleum products into structures on the
property or into the ground, groundwater, or surface water on the property. The findings of this report are
summarized below and may include known or suspected RECs, CRECs, HRECs, VECs, BERs identified
during the performance of this Phase I ESA.

HRECs

     •   Historic Industrial Site Use: Prior to the current use of the SP as the existing solid waste and
         transfer station, the site was used for various industrial operations. Based on Sanborn maps and
         areal images, parts of the SP have been used for industrial operations since 1901. Various uses
         of the SP included the use and storage of hazardous chemicals and petroleum products. The
         following findings are associated with these prior operations:
              o The HIST AST – CA database indicates the historical presence of above-ground storage
                  tanks (ASTs) onsite.
              o The HIST UST – CA database lists two 4,000-gallon underground storage tanks (USTs)
                  of unknown installation date containing regular motor vehicle fuel and a 1,000-gallon UST
                  of unknown installation date containing diesel motor vehicle fuel associated with
                  Clementina Ltd. 1101 – Second St. The exact location of these USTs is unknown;
                  however, based on the address, they were likely associated with the northern portion of
                  the subject property on the parcel identified by APN 60-2382-3-3.
              o At the existing solid waste transfer station 1101 Second Street, the LUST REG 2 – CA
                  database lists a leaky UST site overseen by the Regional Water Quality Control Board
                  (RWQCB). The site had a 350-gallon tank containing waste oil and two tanks of
                  unknown size which contained gasoline and diesel, respectively, that were removed on
                  8/1/1991. The two tanks referenced are likely associated with the HIST USTs cited
                  above. Total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) (gas and diesel), benzene, toluene,
                  xylenes, ethylbenzene, oil and grease, and heavy metals were present in soil and/or
                  groundwater before cleanup. Soil remediation was completed in 1991 after the tanks
                  were removed and three groundwater wells were installed and monitored for one year
                  following removal. After remediation, all compounds were below maximum contaminant
                  levels. The LUST case was closed in a letter dated May 20, 1997. The exact location of
                  this UST is unknown; however, based on the address, they were likely associated with
                  the northern portion of the subject property on the parcel identified by APN 60-2382-3-3..
              o At the Southern Pacific Transportation Company, the LUST REG 2 – CA and
                  LUFT_ALAMEDA COUNTY- CA databases list a leaky UST site overseen by the
                  Alameda County Local Oversight Program. The database lists the case as closed as of
                  8/30/2000. The exact location of this UST is unknown.
              o The Sanborn Maps indicate the presence of former carbide ponds in the same location
                  as the existing transfer station associated with the prior operations of Air Reduction Sales
                  Company. During the site visit, Mr. Gregory Apa indicated that the existing transfer
                  station building and surrounding hardscape surfaces are located in the general vicinity of


                                                      48
                 the former carbide ponds. Mr. Apa based this as what appeared to be lime-treated soil
                 were encountered during asphalt resurfacing activities conducted in November 2016.
                 These carbide ponds could present residual contamination in soil.
       It is the opinion of the environmental professional (EP) that historical industrial use of the SP
       including, but not limited to, the former USTs, ASTs, and carbide ponds, are considered an
       HREC. While there is not a suspicion of specific soil or groundwater contamination, the inherent
       variability of sample results, the size of the SP, and the historic uses, de minimis residual soil
       contamination cannot be ruled out. As such, the EP recommends that, prior to site
       redevelopment, a soil management plan (SMP) be prepared to adequately outline the procedures
       that will be followed to evaluate and remove potentially contaminated soil associated with
       historical operations. At a minimum the SMP should contain a background, recommended field
       screening and soil sampling techniques, proposed soil analytical methods, suspect soil
       segregation procedures, management of identified contaminated soil, and documentation
       protocol.


RECs

   •   10,000-gallon single walled USTs: The UST- CA database lists two 10,000-gallon single-walled
       fiberglass diesel USTs installed on 11/1/1982. The location of these USTs has been denoted on
       Figure 3 with a red X. The last agency listing date was in 2017. During the site visit it was
       confirmed that these USTs are still present onsite. There is a leak system associated with these
       tanks. Due to the age of these USTs and the single-walled construction, regardless of the leak
       detection system, the EP considers a potential release from these tanks to be a REC.
   •   Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) in groundwater: Two immediately upgradient sites and
       one downgradient site of the SP were identified as cleanup sites with VOCs detected in
       groundwater. These sites are all denoted on Figure 3 with yellow Xs. The following summarizes
       these findings:
           o Dove Chemical | Dover Sales | 1X Dover Sales Company, 707 Park Way | 707 Park –
                Upgradient Property
                     The ENVIROSTOR – CA database lists the City of Berkeley as the lead agency
                       on a state response site associated with upgradient property, In Envirostor, the
                       listed contaminants of concern are xylenes, benzene, 1- butanol, vinyl chloride,
                       toluene, and hydrocarbon solvents. The City of Berkeley became the lead
                       agency and was monitoring groundwater on 8/29/2002. On 11/22/1989 it is
                       certified that seven USTs were removed from the site. These USTs contained
                       the following compounds: toluene, methyl ethyl ketone (2-butanone), xylenes,
                       mineral spirits (paint-related materials), lactol spirits (petroleum naptha), special
                       naptholite 66/3, and a mixture of these chemicals.
                     Records in the HIST UST – CA database indicate seven historical USTs:
                            •   three 550-gallon USTs with unknown installation dates containing
                                toluene (methylbenzene, aromatic hydrocarbon low analine), isopropyl
                                alcohol (2- propanol) and xylenes, respectively;
                            •   two 4,000-gallon USTs with unknown installation dates containing
                                Chevron 265 thinner and aliphatic 225 thinner, respectively;



                                                    49
                •    one 6000- gallon UST with an unknown installation date containing
                     methyl ethyl ketone (2-butanone);
                • one 2,000-gallon UST with an unknown installation date containing
                     toluene (methylbenzene, aromatic hydrocarbon low analine), isopropyl
                     alcohol (2-propanol), xylenes, and methyl ethyl ketone (2-butanone).
                In records associated with the HIST UST – CA database, leaks were
                detected in all these tanks by both visual inspection and stock inventory on
                records from 5/27/1989. According to Envirostor records, when the tanks
                were removed, hydrocarbons were discovered in soil and groundwater and
                three monitoring wells were installed. Annual groundwater monitoring has
                been conducted since 1990. Geotracker lists this case as closed as of
                7/24/2000.

o   Terminal Manufacturing Co. LLC, 707 Gilman St– Upgradient Property

           The SLIC REG 2 – CA database lists this upgradient property as an open
            remediation site. The San Francisco Bay RWQCB is the lead oversite agency on
            this site. Potential media of concern is groundwater and soil vapor and potential
            contaminants of concern on this site are listed as diesel, gasoline, and
            tetrachloroethene. The most recent monitoring report available on Geotracker,
            Enhanced In-Situ Bioremediation Injection Program Monitoring Report – 707
            Gilman Street – Berkeley, California (RMD Environmental Solutions, 2021),
            shows groundwater concentrations of PCE in shallow groundwater (less than 25
            ft below ground surface [bgs]) from samples collected on 10/8/2020 and
            12/18/2020 as high as 106 ug/L and samples collected on the same days from
            deeper groundwater (greater than 25 ft bgs) at concentrations as high as 1,920
            ug/L, exceeding commercial environmental screening levels established by the
            RWQCB. These sample locations are on the western edge of the upgradient
            property, directly upgradient from the SP. TCE, vinyl chloride, cis-1,2-DCE, and
            other VOCs exceed and have also exceeded ESLs in sample from this site. Due
            to the concentrations of VOCs and the groundwater flow direction, it is
            reasonable to believe that groundwater beneath the subject property has been
            affected by this upgradient property.

o   Weatherford Inc DBA Weatherford Collision Center North | AT&T Mobility | Hawkins
    Traffic Safety Supply, 1255 East Shore Hwy. | 1225 E Shore Hwy – Downgradient
    Property
         The SLIC REG 2 – CA database lists this property as a downgradient site,
             which is a cleanup site eligible for closure. The site contaminants of concern
             (COCs) are listed as Dichloroethene (DCE), Trichloroethylene (TCE), Vinyl
             chloride, Ethylbenzene, and Gasoline. The site is listed as eligible for closure
             because concentrations of VOCs are believed to be from an upgradient off-site
             source. The most recent monitoring report available on Geotracker, Fourth
             Quarter 2019 Groundwater Monitoring/ Fall Indoor Air Sampling Report and Low-
             Threat Closure Assessment, Former Hawkins Traffic Safety Supply - 1255
             Eastshore Highway - Berkeley, CA (PIERS Environmental Services, 2020),


                                       50
                         shows concentrations of VOCs are present in groundwater. Indoor air was also
                         sampled on this site and concentrations of various VOCs exceed the commercial
                         indoor air environmental screening level.
        Collectively, these findings present a strong case for the presence of VOCs in groundwater
        underneath the SP, particularly the southern part of the SP. The EP considers the potential
        presence of VOCs in groundwater in the subsurface of the SP to be a REC. Potential for
        contaminated groundwater under the site also presents a VEC on the SP. Based on this
        designation and the intention of this Phase I ESA to evaluate the site for future development, the
        EP recommends sub-slab vapor sampling and/or soil gas sampling associated with plans for
        future closed structures on the site.

BERs:
Industrial operations associated with the current use of the subject property present a number of BERs.

    •   Truck Wash: The Phase I ESA completed in 2021 by Environmental Assessment Specialists
        identified a truck wash area with an oil water separator onsite. This area was noted during the site
        visit by Cameron-Cole personnel and is denoted in Figure 3. There is no evidence that any
        release has occurred associated with these operations and the oil water separator. The
        operation of this truck wash area is a BER because if the oil water separator were to fail or the
        concrete and asphalt surface was to have a penetration, there is potential for oil, grease, solvent,
        and petroleum products to be released to the environment.
    •   Vehicle Maintenance Building and Service Bays: The City of Berkeley operates large vehicle
        maintenance and repair facility with four service bays on the subject property adjacent to the
        transfer station, denoted in Figure 3. Various hazardous substances and petroleum products are
        associated with vehicle maintenance operations. No drains, sumps, in ground lifts, or other
        penetrations in the slab were noted in this area during the site inspection. The operations of this
        maintenance and repair facility presents a BER due the potential for release due to the use of
        hazardous substances and petroleum products.
    •   Hazardous Waste Collection: Though the existing transfer station does not accept hazardous
        waste, some hazardous waste is inadvertently present in wastes that are brought to the property.
        Typically, this hazardous waste is sorted and stored in a separate area before it is removed from
        the subject property. The storage of this hazardous waste on the SP represents a BER.
    •   Stormwater Collection System: A large sump area with fitted Baker Tank located north of the
        transfer station area on the subject property (denoted on Figure 3 with a blue X as “stormwater
        holding AST”). Stormwater that does not qualify to be discharged directly to the municipal
        stormwater system is stored and discharged to domestic sewer (EBMUD) through industrial use
        permit. The entire site is capped by concrete of asphalt surfaces and has a sophisticated
        stormwater collection system that is permitted through the state of California. Stormwater on the
        subject property likely comes into contact with wastes that are stored on the subject property
        during operations. The stormwater collection system presents a BER because if there is a leak or
        malfunction of the system there is a potential for a release of hazardous stormwater to the
        environment.

Although there is no evidence of a release associated with the BERs described listed above, operation of
these BERs may have resulted in de minimis soil contamination near these features. Prior to



                                                    51
development and subsurface excavation, a property-wide SMP (discussed previously for the HRECs)
should be completed.

             Description :

                    For designated operator (DO) monthly inspections conducted before October 1, 2018, failure to comply with one or
                    more of the following requirements: Be performed by an ICC certified DO. Inspect monthly alarm history report,
                    check that alarms are documented and responded to appropriately, and attach a copy. Inspect for the presence of
                    liquid/debris in spill containers. Inspect for the presence of liquid/debris in under dispenser containment (UDC) and
                    ensure that the monitoring equipment is positioned correctly. Inspect for liquid or debris in containment sumps
                    where an alarm occurred with no service visit. Check that all testing and maintenance has been completed and
                    documented. Verify that all facility employees have been trained in accordance with 23 CCR 2715(c). For
                    designated operator (DO) 30 day inspections conducted on and after October 1, 2018, failure to conduct the
                    designated UST operator visual inspection at least once every 30 days.


             Notes :

                    Returned to compliance on 11/23/2021. The 12/8/2020 Designated UST Operator Visual Inspection Report (DO
                    Report) notes T2 spill bucket was found with a mixture of fuel and water. The 8/12/2021 DO Report notes a mixture
                    of diesel and water found in UDC 1/2. There is no owner/operator description of follow-up action on either DO
                    Report. The 10/13/2020, 11/9/2020, 12/8/2020, 1/5/2020, 8/12/2021 and 9/8/2021 Designated UST Operator Visual
                    Inspection Reports are not signed by the Owner/Operator acknowledging the results of the DO inspection.
                    Corrective action: Provide TMD with the follow-up action taken on the fuel and water in the T2 spill bucket and the
                    diesel and water found in UDC 1, and document on the report. The owner/operator shall review, sign and date the
                    Designated UST Operator Visual Inspection Reports that are not signed and shall sign and date the reports within

      Source Description

              Source Description :

                     The NPDES module of the Compliance Information System (ICIS) tracks surface water permits issued under the
                     Clean Water Act. Under NPDES, all facilities that discharge pollutants from any point source into waters of the
                     United States are required to obtain a permit. The permit will likely contain limits on what can be discharged,
                     impose monitoring and reporting requirements, and include other provisions to ensure that the discharge does not
                     adversely affect water quality.

      Source Description

              Source Description :

                     The California Environmental Protection Agency (CalEPA) has recently implemented a new data warehouse system
                     (nSite). This data warehouse combines and merges facility and site information from five different systems
                     managed within CalEPA. The five systems are: California Environmental Reporting System (CERS), EnviroStor,
                     GeoTracker, California Integrated Water Quality System (CIWQS), and Toxic Release Inventory (TRI).

      Source Description
            Source Description :                         ICIS provides a database that, when complete, will contain enforcement
                                                         and compliance information across most of EPA's programs. The vision
                                                         for ICIS is to replace EPA's independent databases that contain
                                                         enforcement data with a single repository for that information.
                                                         Currently, ICIS contains all Federal Administrative and Judicial
                                                         enforcement actions and a subset of the Permit Compliance System
                                                         (PCS), which supports the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination
                                                         System (NPDES). This information is maintained in ICIS by EPA in the
                                                         Regional offices and at Headquarters. A future release of ICIS will
                                                         completely replace PCS and will integrate that information with Federal
                                                         actions already in the system. ICIS also has the capability to track other
                                                         activities that support compliance and enforcement programs, including
                                                         incident tracking, compliance assistance, and compliance monitoring.
                                                         The NPDES module of the Compliance Information System (ICIS) tracks
                                                         surface water permits issued under the Clean Water Act. Under NPDES,
                                                         all facilities that discharge pollutants from any point source into waters
                                                         of the United States are required to obtain a permit. The permit will
                                                         likely contain limits on what can be discharged, impose monitoring and
                                                         reporting requirements, and include other provisions to ensure that the
                                                         discharge does not adversely affect water quality.

              Source Description :

                     The Emission Inventory System (EIS) maintains an inventory of large stationary sources and voluntarily-reported
                     smaller sources of air point pollution emitters. It contains information about facility sites and their physical location,
                     emission units, emission processes, release points, control approaches, and regulations. Facility inventory data are
                     kept separate from the emissions data and have stable identifiers to improve continuity from year to year and to
                     help identify duplicate or missing facilities.

      Source Description

             Source Description :

                    The California Environmental Protection Agency (CalEPA) has recently implemented a new data warehouse system
                    (nSite). This data warehouse combines and merges facility and site information from five different systems
                    managed within CalEPA. The five systems are: California Environmental Reporting System (CERS), EnviroStor,
                    GeoTracker, California Integrated Water Quality System (CIWQS), and Toxic Release Inventory (TRI).


             Source Description :

                    RCRAInfo is EPA’s comprehensive information system that supports the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
                    (RCRA) of 1976 and the Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments (HSWA) of 1984 through the tracking of events
                    and activities related to facilities that generate, transport, and treat, store, or dispose of hazardous waste.
                    RCRAInfo allows RCRA program staff to track the notification, permit, compliance, and corrective action activities
                    required under RCRA. RCRAInfo also supports generation of the National Hazardous Waste Biennial Report. All
                    generators and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities who handle hazardous waste are required to report to
                    the EPA Administrator at least once every two years to support creation of the Biennial Report.

      Source Description

             Source Description :

                    smaller sources of air point pollution emitters. It contains information about facility sites and their physical location,
                    emission units, emission processes, release points, control approaches, and regulations. Facility inventory data are
                    kept separate from the emissions data and have stable identifiers to improve continuity from year to year and to
                    help identify duplicate or missing facilities.

              Source Description :

                     RCRAInfo is EPA’s comprehensive information system that supports the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
                     (RCRA) of 1976 and the Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments (HSWA) of 1984 through the tracking of events
                     and activities related to facilities that generate, transport, and treat, store, or dispose of hazardous waste.
                     RCRAInfo allows RCRA program staff to track the notification, permit, compliance, and corrective action activities
                     required under RCRA. RCRAInfo also supports generation of the National Hazardous Waste Biennial Report. All
                     generators and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities who handle hazardous waste are required to report to
                     the EPA Administrator at least once every two years to support creation of the Biennial Report.

               Source Description :

                      RCRAInfo is EPA’s comprehensive information system that supports the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
                      (RCRA) of 1976 and the Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments (HSWA) of 1984 through the tracking of events
                      and activities related to facilities that generate, transport, and treat, store, or dispose of hazardous waste.
                      RCRAInfo allows RCRA program staff to track the notification, permit, compliance, and corrective action activities
                      required under RCRA. RCRAInfo also supports generation of the National Hazardous Waste Biennial Report. All
                      generators and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities who handle hazardous waste are required to report to
                      the EPA Administrator at least once every two years to support creation of the Biennial Report.

       Source Description

               Source Description :

                      RCRAInfo is EPA’s comprehensive information system that supports the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
                      (RCRA) of 1976 and the Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments (HSWA) of 1984 through the tracking of events
                      and activities related to facilities that generate, transport, and treat, store, or dispose of hazardous waste.
                      RCRAInfo allows RCRA program staff to track the notification, permit, compliance, and corrective action activities
                      required under RCRA. RCRAInfo also supports generation of the National Hazardous Waste Biennial Report. All
                      generators and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities who handle hazardous waste are required to report to
                      the EPA Administrator at least once every two years to support creation of the Biennial Report.

       Source Description

               Source Description :

                      The California Environmental Protection Agency (CalEPA) has recently implemented a new data warehouse system
                      (nSite). This data warehouse combines and merges facility and site information from five different systems
                      managed within CalEPA. The five systems are: California Environmental Reporting System (CERS), EnviroStor,
                      GeoTracker, California Integrated Water Quality System (CIWQS), and Toxic Release Inventory (TRI).


               Source Description :

                      The Emission Inventory System (EIS) maintains an inventory of large stationary sources and voluntarily-reported
                      smaller sources of air point pollution emitters. It contains information about facility sites and their physical location,
                      emission units, emission processes, release points, control approaches, and regulations. Facility inventory data are
                      kept separate from the emissions data and have stable identifiers to improve continuity from year to year and to
                      help identify duplicate or missing facilities.

       Source Description

               Source Description :

                      RCRAInfo is EPA’s comprehensive information system that supports the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
                      (RCRA) of 1976 and the Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments (HSWA) of 1984 through the tracking of events
                      and activities related to facilities that generate, transport, and treat, store, or dispose of hazardous waste.
                      RCRAInfo allows RCRA program staff to track the notification, permit, compliance, and corrective action activities
                      required under RCRA. RCRAInfo also supports generation of the National Hazardous Waste Biennial Report. All
                      generators and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities who handle hazardous waste are required to report to
                      the EPA Administrator at least once every two years to support creation of the Biennial Report.

ENVIROSTOR - CA (cont.)

               Document Type :                                  Certification

               Comments :

                      Completed RA. Seven underground storage tanks (USTs) were removed from the site. The USTs contained toluene,
                      methyl ethyl ketone (2-butanone), xylenes, mineral spirits (paint-related materials), lactol spirits (petroleum
                      naptha), special naptholite 66/3, and a mixture of these chemicals. Hydrocarbons were discovered in soil and
                      groundwater during tank removal, and three monitoring wells were installed on March 30, 1990. Analysis of soil
                      samples collected during the groundwater monitoring well installation indicated up to 1,800 parts per million (ppm)
                      toluene, 24 ppm ethylbenzene, 77 ppm xylenes and 3.6 ppm chlorobenzene. Annual groundwater monitoring had
                      been conducted since 1990 and the City of Berkeley received all reports. In general, groundwater concentration
                      levels had dropped: toluene (21,000 ppb in 1990 to 25 ppb in 2001), benzene (610 ppb in 1990 to 15 ppb in 2001),
                      ethylbenzene (310 ppb in 1990 to 1.3 ppb in 2001), total xylenes (420 ppb in 1990 to 9.8 ppb in 2001), and TPH
                      gas (370,000 ppb in 1990 to 310 ppb in 2001).


               Completed Date :                                 1984-04-17
               Area Name :                                      PROJECT WIDE
               Sub Area Name :                                  N/R
               Document Type :                                  Removal Action Completion Report

               Comments :

                      Completed RA. On July 12, 1983 the Department of Health Services (DHS), predecessor to Department of Toxic
                      Substances Control (DTSC), in response to an employee s complaint, inspected the Dover Sales (DS) and Precision
                      Technical Coating (PTC) site. Soil samples taken from the DS site found 2-butanone, 1-butanol and various alkanes
                      and aromatics. Cleanup of the site started on January 26, 1984, and a total of about 26 cubic yards of
                      contaminated soil removed. DHS determined that the site cleanup had been completed.

       Source Description

               Source Description :

                      known contamination or sites for which there may be reasons to investigate further. The EnviroStor database
                      includes the following site types: Federal Superfund sites (National Priorities List (NPL)); State Response, including

               Source Description :

                      RCRAInfo is EPA’s comprehensive information system that supports the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
                      (RCRA) of 1976 and the Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments (HSWA) of 1984 through the tracking of events
                      and activities related to facilities that generate, transport, and treat, store, or dispose of hazardous waste.
                      RCRAInfo allows RCRA program staff to track the notification, permit, compliance, and corrective action activities
                      required under RCRA. RCRAInfo also supports generation of the National Hazardous Waste Biennial Report. All
                      generators and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities who handle hazardous waste are required to report to
                      the EPA Administrator at least once every two years to support creation of the Biennial Report.

       Source Description

               Source Description :

                      RCRAInfo is EPA’s comprehensive information system that supports the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
                      (RCRA) of 1976 and the Hazardous and Solid Waste Amendments (HSWA) of 1984 through the tracking of events
                      and activities related to facilities that generate, transport, and treat, store, or dispose of hazardous waste.
                      RCRAInfo allows RCRA program staff to track the notification, permit, compliance, and corrective action activities
                      required under RCRA. RCRAInfo also supports generation of the National Hazardous Waste Biennial Report. All
                      generators and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities who handle hazardous waste are required to report to
                      the EPA Administrator at least once every two years to support creation of the Biennial Report.
