                                        APPENDIX G
      Stellar Environmental Standard Procedures for
                 Groundwater Monitoring




Stellar Environmental Solutions, Inc.
STELLAR ENVIRONMENTAL SOLUTIONS, INC.
STANDARD GROUNDWATER SAMPLING PROTOCOLS
IMPLEMENTED BY BLAINE TECH SERVICES


SAMPLING AND ANALYSIS PERSONNEL

Sampling and analysis was conducted by Blaine Tech Services, a subcontractor to Stellar
Environmental, which used appropriately trained personnel to perform the water level
measurements, sampling, and analyses of key natural attenuation indicators.

SUMMARY OF SAMPLING PROCEDURES

Groundwater sampling activities include:
    Pre-arrangement with testing laboratory
    Assembly and preparation of equipment and supplies
    Groundwater sampling
        water-level measurements
        immiscible material measurements (with an interface probe, if applicable)
        visual inspection of borehole water
        well bore evacuation
        sampling
    Sample preservation and shipment
        sample preparation
        onsite measurement of parameters using direct-read instruments
        sample labeling
    Completion of sample records
    Completion of chain-of-custody records
    Samples placed in chilled cooler
    Sample shipment



Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
ARRANGEMENTS WITH ANALYTICAL LABORATORY

Prior to sampling, arrangements will be made with E, an analytical laboratory in Berkeley,
California. EA has the required Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) certification to
perform the analyses, and will provide a sufficient number of sample containers for the wells to
be sampled and the blanks to be included. EA will determine the proper type and size for the
containers based on the analyses requested. For samples requiring chemical preservation,
preservatives will be added to containers by the EA prior to shipping containers to the facility.
Shipping containers (ice chests with adequate container padding) will be sent to the facility with
the sample containers.

PREPARATION FOR SAMPLING

Prior to the sampling episode, equipment to be used will be assembled and its operating
condition verified, calibrated (if required), and properly cleaned (if required). In addition, all
record-keeping materials will be prepared.

Equipment Calibration

Where appropriate, equipment will be calibrated according to the manufacturer’s specifications
prior to field use. This applies to the equipment for making onsite chemical measurements of pH,
conductivity, water temperature, and dissolved oxygen (DO)

Equipment Cleaning

Portions of sampling and test equipment that will come into contact with the sample will be
thoroughly cleaned before use. Such equipment includes water-level probe, bailers, lifting line,
and other equipment or portions thereof that may be immersed. The following procedure will be
used for cleaning non-dedicated equipment:
    Clean with potable water and phosphate-free detergent;
    Rinse with potable water;
    Rinse with distilled or deionized water; and
    Airs dry the equipment prior to use.

Any deviations from these procedures will be documented in the permanent record of the
sampling event.

Laboratory-supplied sample containers will be cleaned and sealed by the laboratory before
shipping. The type of container provided and the method of container cleaning should be in the
laboratory’s permanent record of the sampling event.



Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
Used sampling equipment to be disposed of will be cleaned with potable water and phosphate-
free detergent before disposal as solid waste. Rinse water will be stored in properly labeled 55-
gallon drums for proper disposal, pending receipt of laboratory results of groundwater and soil
sample analyses with assistance from Stellar Environmental.

SAMPLING PROCEDURES

Special care will be exercised to prevent contamination of the groundwater and extracted
samples during the sampling activities. Contamination of a sample can occur through contact
with improperly cleaned equipment. Cross-contamination of the groundwater can occur through
insufficient cleaning of equipment between wells. Pre-cleaned disposable sampling equipment
will be rinsed with distilled water prior to use. Sampling equipment and sample containers will
be thoroughly cleaned before and after field use and between uses at different sampling locations
according to the procedures discussed above. In addition to the use of properly cleaned
equipment, two further precautions will be taken:
    A new pair of clean, disposable latex (or similar) gloves will be worn each time a different
       well is sampled.
    Sample collection activities will progress from the least affected (upgradient) area to the
       most affected (downgradient) area. Wells described as “background” or “upgradient”
       wells will be sampled first.

The following paragraphs present procedures for the several activities that comprise groundwater
sample acquisition. These activities will be performed in the same order as presented below.
Exceptions to this procedure will be noted in the permanent sampling record.

Preparation of Location

Prior to starting the sampling procedure, the area around the well will be cleared of foreign
materials, such as brush, rocks, and debris. A clean (new) disposable plastic sheet will be placed
around the well casing so that the sheet is flat on the ground. The sheet will be placed such that
the flush-mount well projects through the center of the sheet. This preparation will prevent
sampling equipment from inadvertently contacting the ground or exterior parts of the well.

Water-Level Measurement

The first sampling operation will involve measurement of the water level. An electrical probe or
a weighted tape will be used to measure the depth to groundwater below the datum to the nearest
0.01 foot. The datum, usually the top of the inner casing (inside and below the protective steel
cover), will be described in the monitoring well records. A permanent mark or scribe will be
marked on the inner casing.



Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
If the wells to be sampled are closely spaced, the water levels at all of the closely-spaced wells
will be measured before any of the wells are evacuated. The water-level probe or weighted tape
will be cleaned with phosphate-free detergent in distilled water and with a distilled water rinse
between uses at different wells.

Total Depth Measurement

Once the water level and immiscible material thickness are measured and recorded, the water-
level probe or weighted tape will be slowly lowered to the bottom of the well. The depth to
bottom will be measured and recorded. The probe or tape will then be slowly withdrawn from
the well. The bottom of the probe or tape will be observed after withdrawal for any evidence of
viscous, heavy contaminants. Descriptions (and measurements, if possible) of such materials will
be made from observation of the probe or tape.

Visual Inspection of Well Water

Prior to well evacuation, a small quantity of water will be removed with a bailer that is not
completely immersed. The recovered sample is representative of the top of the water column in
the well casing. If immiscible materials are present as measured by the interface probe at the top
of the water column, this technique can allow their detection. The water will be observed for the
presence of any floating films or other indications of immiscible materials. Any sample odors
will be noted. Observations regarding odor or visual evidence of immiscible materials will be
recorded in the sampling record.

The well water sample will be discarded unless the site-specific protocol calls for retention of
this sample. The sample will be placed in a labeled container for proper disposal.

Well Bore Evacuation

Water contained within and adjacent to the well casing can potentially reflect chemical
interaction with the atmosphere (by diffusion of gases down the casing) or the well construction
materials (through prolonged residence adjacent to the casing).

Observations of this water will be recorded during removal and prior to it being discarded.
Onsite parameter measurements of the purged water, as described in this section, will indicate
when water-quality parameters have stabilized, and also will be recorded.

The volume of water contained within the well bore at the time of sampling will be calculated,
and 4 times the calculated water volume will be removed from the well and discarded. A bailer
will be used for well evacuation. The volume of water to be evacuated will be calculated as
follows:



Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
Number of Bailers:

                                       Volume of water in well (Vw)
          Number of bailers = 4 x
                                          Volume of bailer (Vb)

Volume of Water in Well:

       Vw = 3.142 x dw2 x Lw

                   4



        where:          Vw = water volume in well (ft3)

                        dw = inside diameter of well (ft)

                        Lw = length of water column in well (ft)



Volume of Water in Full Bailer:

       Vb = 3.142 x db2 x Lb

                   4



        where:          Vb = water volume in bailer (ft3)

                        db = inside diameter of bailer (ft)

                        Lb = length of bailer (ft)



Wells that can be evacuated to a dry state will be evacuated completely; samples will be taken as
soon as groundwater has recovered to 80 percent of its original volume or until sufficient water
for sampling is present. Sample compositing—sampling over a lengthy period by accumulating
small volumes of water at different times to eventually obtain a sample of sufficient volume—
will not be conducted.




Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
Water produced during well evacuation will be contained in a suitable container and temporarily
stored onsite pending proper disposal.

Some chemical and physical parameters in water can change significantly within a short time of
sample acquisition. The following parameters cannot be accurately measured in a laboratory
located more than a few hours from the facility, and will be measured onsite with portable
equipment:
    pH
    Specific conductance
    Temperature
    Turbidity units

These parameters will be measured in unfiltered, unpreserved, “fresh” water, using the same
sampling technique as for laboratory analyses. The measurements will be made in a clean glass
container separate from those intended for laboratory analyses. The tested sample will be
discarded after use. The measured values will be recorded in the sampling record.

Natural Attenuation Field Measurements

In addition to the meter reading above, following the indicators that groundwater has been
purged sufficiently to represent water within the water-bearing materials, natural attenuation
parameters were measured by the Blaine Tech sampling personnel. These include meter readings
for:
    Oxidation reduction potential
    Dissolved oxygen

Sample Extraction

Natural attenuation parameters are measured after groundwater is purged, prior to the collection
of samples. Care will be taken during insertion of sampling equipment to prevent undue
disturbance of water in the well.

The bailer will be lowered into the water gently to prevent splashing, and extracted gently to
prevent creation of excessive disturbance or aeration in the well. The sample will be transferred
directly into the appropriate container. While pouring water from a bailer, the water will be
carefully poured down the inside of the sample bottle to prevent significant aeration of the
sample. Unless other instructions are given by the analytical laboratory, the sample containers
will be completely filled so that no air space remains in the container. Excess water taken during
sampling will be placed in a container for proper disposal.


Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
SAMPLE HANDLING

Sample Preservation

Water samples will be properly prepared for transportation to the laboratory by refrigeration and
chemical preservation, as necessary. The laboratory providing sample containers will add any
necessary chemical preservatives to the sealed containers provided prior to shipment.

Container and Labels

Glass containers and appropriate container lids will be provided by the laboratory. The
containers will be filled and container lids tightly closed. Sample container lids will be sealed so
as to make obvious any seal tampered with or broken. The label will be firmly attached to the
container side (rather than the lid). The following information will be written with permanent
marker on the label:
    Facility name
    Sample identification
    Sample type (groundwater, surface water, etc.)
    Sampling date
    Sampling time
    Preservatives added, and sample collector’s initials

Sample Shipment

Samples for this project will be delivered directly to EA laboratory under chain of custody
control. The concentration and type of compounds present in the groundwater are considered by
the U.S. Department of Transportation to be non-hazardous. Thus, should samples be required to
be shipped to a laboratory, the following packaging and labeling requirements for the sample
materials are appropriate for shipping the sample to the testing laboratory:
    Package sample so that is does not leak, spill, or vaporize from its packaging.
    Label package with:
        Sample collector’s name, address, and telephone number
        Laboratory’s name, address, and telephone number
        Description of sample
        Quantity of sample
        Date of shipment




Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
To comply with packaging regulations and prevent damage to expensive groundwater samples,
Stellar Environmental will follow the packaging and shipping instructions supplied by the
certified testing laboratory.

Chain-of-Custody Control

After samples are obtained, chain-of-custody procedures will be followed to establish a written
record concerning sample movement between the sampling site and the testing laboratory. Each
shipping container will contain a chain-of-custody form to be completed by the sampling
personnel packing the samples. The chain-of-custody form for each container will be completed
in triplicate. One copy of this form will be maintained at the site; the other two copies will
remain at the laboratory. One of the laboratory copies will become a part of the permanent record
for the sample and will be returned with the sample analyses.

The record will contain the following minimum information:
    Collector’s sample number
    Signature of collector
    Date and time of collection
    Place and address of collection
    Material type
    Preservatives added
    Analyses requested
    Signatures involved in the chain of possession
    Inclusive dates of possession

The shipping container will be maintained under the immediate control of Blaine Tech staff for
delivery to EA Laboratory. In the event of shat samples will be shipped or transferred by courier
the shipping container shall be sealed so as to make obvious any seal tampered with or broken.
The chain-of-custody documentation will be placed inside the container so that it is immediately
apparent to the laboratory personnel receiving the container, but could not be damaged or lost
during shipping.

SAMPLING RECORDS

To provide complete documentation of sampling, detailed records containing the following
information will be maintained during sampling:
    Sample location (facility name)


Stellar Environmental Solution, Inc.
    Sample identification (name and sample number)
    Sample location map or detailed sketch
    Date and time of sampling
    Sampling method
    Field observations of sample appearance and odor
    Weather conditions
    Samples identification
    Any other significant information

Section 4: Fire and Explosion Data
FLAMMABILITY CLASSIFICATION: Combustible Liquid - Class IIIB.
FLASHPOINT: Greater than 320F (160 C).
EXTINGUISHING MEDIA: Water, CO2, dry chemical, foam, sand.
UNUSUAL FIRE AND EXPLOSION HAZARDS: Rags soaked with any oil or solvent can present a fire
hazard and should always be stored in UL Listed or Factory Mutual approved, covered containers.
Improperly stored rags can create conditions that lead to oxidation. Oxidation, under certain conditions
can lead to spontaneous combustion.


Section 5: Reactivity Data
STABILITY: Generally stable. Spontaneous combustion can occur. See Unusual Fire and Explosion
Procedures, Section IV.

CONDITIONS TO AVOID: High surface area exposure to oxygen can result in polymerization and release
of heat.

INCOMPATABILITY (MATERIALS TO AVOID): Avoid contact with strong oxidizing agents.

HAZARDOUS DECOMPOSITIONS OR BY-PRODUCTS: Decomposition may produce carbon dioxide
and carbon monoxide.

HAZARDOUS POLYMERIZATION: Will not occur.


Section 6: Health Hazard Data
THRESHHOLD LIMIT VALUE: As a liquid - none. As oil mist - 10 mg/m3 total particulate.

INHALATION HEALTH RISKS AND SYMPTOMS OF EXPOSURE: Excessive inhalation of oil mist may
affect the respiratory system. Oil mist is classified as a nuisance particulate by ACGIH.

SKIN ABSORPTION HEALTH RISKS AND SYMPTOMS OF EXPOSURE: Not classified as a primary
skin irritant or corrosive material. Sensitive individuals may experience dermatitis after long exposure of
oil on skin.

HEALTH HAZARDS (ACUTE AND CHRONIC): Acute: none observed by inhalation. Chronic: none
reported.

EMERGENCY AND FIRST AID PROCEDURES FOR:

SKIN CONTACT: May be removed from skin by washing with soap and warm water.

EYE CONTACT: Immediately flush eyes with plenty of cool water for at least 15 minutes. Do NOT let
victim rub eyes.

INHALATION: Immediately remove exposed individual to fresh air source. If victim has stopped breathing
give artificial respiration, get medical attention immediately.




Material Safety Data Sheet                                                          Rev. Date: January 21, 2012
Page 2
Material Safety Data Sheet


Section 7: Precautions for Safe Handling and Use
ENVIRONMENTAL PRECAUTIONS: Where large spills are possible, a comprehensive spill response
plan should be developed and implemented.

STEPS TO BE TAKEN IN CASE MATERIAL IS RELEASED OR SPILLED: Wear appropriate respiratory
protection and protective clothing as described in Section 8. Depending on quantity of spill: (a) Small
spill: Add solid adsorbent, shovel into disposable container and wash the area. Clean area with
detergent. (b) Large spill: Squeegee or pump into holding container. Clean area with detergent. In the
event of an uncontrolled release of this material, the user should determine if this release is reportable
under applicable laws and regulations.

WASTE DISPOSAL METHOD: All recovered material should be packaged, labeled, transported, and
disposed or reclaimed in accordance with local, state, and federal regulations and good engineering
practices.


Section 8: Control Measures
RESPIRATORY PROTECTION: Not normally needed. A qualified health specialist should evaluate
whether there is a need for respiratory protection under specific conditions.

VENTILATION: Handle in the presence of adequate ventilation. Intermittent clean air exchanges
recommended, but not required.

PROTECTIVE GLOVES: Not normally needed. However, protective clothing is always recommended
when handling chemicals.

EYE PROTECTION: Eye protection is always recommended when handling chemicals. Wear safety
glasses meeting the specifications established in ANSI Standard Z87.1.


Section 9: Special Precautions
PRECAUTIONS TO BE TAKEN IN HANDLING AND STORAGE: Store away from flame, fire, and
excessive heat.


Section 10: Disposal Considerations
General Information: Do not discharge into drains, watercourses or onto the ground. Discharge,
treatment, or disposal may be subject to national, state, or local laws. Empty containers may contain
product residues.

Disposal Methods: No specific disposal method required.

Container: Since emptied containers retain product residue, follow label warnings even after container is
emptied.

                   Tech Brief                                                                       Tersus Environmental
                                                                                   For every zone of your plume, we’ve got you covered!
                   Enhanced Anaerobic Bioremediation



     EDS-ER™
     Electron Donor Solution – Extended Release
     As delivered, the physical state of EDS-ER™ (electron donor solution – extended release) by Tersus Environmental is
     significantly different than standard emulsified vegetable oil (EVO) products. Whereas other EVO products are
     concentrated emulsions containing water, EDS-ER™ is a water-mixable oil; it contains no water. Thus, the costs for
     shipping EDS-ER are about 50% less than conventional products.

     At room temperature, EDS-ER™ is a liquid material with an appearance and viscosity roughly equivalent to vegetable oil.
     Unlike common EVO products, EDS-ER™ will not separate, will not freeze, and has a shelf life of 2 years without spoilage.

     Tersus Environmental is proud to announce that EDS-ER™ does NOT contain ethoxylated surfactants. As you may know,
     many environmental remediation injectates, such as emulsified vegetable oils use biodegradable non-ionic surfactants.
     Unfortunately, ethoxylation, the manufacturing process that creates these surfactants (e.g., polysorbates) often results in
     these products containing 1,4-dioxane.

SUBJECT: Conditional Approval of Workplan for Additional Activities, and
         Requests for Reports, Terminal Manufacturing Co., 707 Gilman
         Street, Berkeley, Alameda County

Dear Mr. Mellinger:

This letter conditionally approves the July 26, 2021, Closure Criteria Evaluation &
Workplan for Additional Activities submitted by your consultant RMD Environmental
Solutions (RMD). This letter also requests that Terminal Manufacturing Company (TMC)
submits reports documenting the completion of the proposed work.

Background
RMD, on behalf of TMC, conducted groundwater treatment injections in December 2019
near three former sumps to treat areas with high concentrations of tetrachloroethene
(PCE). The high concentration areas represented remaining secondary source of
contamination. Groundwater monitoring near two of the sumps indicates substantial
improvement in PCE concentration after treatment injections using emulsified vegetable
oil. There are no monitoring wells adjacent to the third sump so concentrations in this
area are not known. The Workplan includes a data review using the 2009 Assessment
Tool for Closure of Low-Threat Chlorinated Solvent Sites and proposes ways to meet
Low-Threat closure needs identified during the review.

Workplan Summary
Additional groundwater remediation, improved delineation of the groundwater plume,
additional monitoring to establish plume stability or degradation, and additional soil
vapor and indoor air sampling are needed for Low-Threat closure. As reported in the
Workplan there is no current PCE exposure. The Workplan proposes:

                     J1M M c G RATH, CHAIR     I M ICHA EL M ONTGOMERY, EXECUTIVE OFFICER
             1515 Clay St., Suite 1400, Oakla nd , CA 94612   I www .waterboards .ca .gov/sanfranclscobay
File No.: 01S0773                                                               Page 2 of 3


      Sampling seven existing sub-slab vapor probes;
      Sampling indoor air again based on the results of the sub-slab vapor sampling;
      Installing two additional pairs of shallow and deeper groundwater monitoring
       wells;
      Conduct additional groundwater treatment injections using four to six new
       injection points;
      Sampling the existing and new wells on a quarterly basis for one year following
       additional groundwater treatment.

Conditional Approval
I approve the Workplan subject to the following conditions:
     Sample well MW-16, with reported PCE up to 120 µg/L when it was last sampled
       in 2015.
     Contact the City of Berkeley Toxic Management Division for the proposed well
       destruction proposed in Section 4.2.1.

Reporting Requests
TMC is requested to incorporate the above conditions into the proposed work and
submit a completion report by January 31, 2022. The report shall document completion
of the conditionally approved workplan tasks and present implementation results. The
report should include the following element(s):

      Results of the sub-slab vapor and indoor air sampling;
      Well installation description, boring logs, well survey data;
      Description of the supplemental treatment injections, and the first round of post
       injection groundwater sampling; and
      Results presented on both figures and in tables.

TMC is requested to submit an annual groundwater monitoring and treatment injections
performance evaluation report by January 31, 2023, and include the groundwater flow
direction and gradient in the surveyed area. The report should include:
     Source Property map;
     Sampling location map and sample results maps;
     Sampling methods;
     Analytical analyses and concentration trend graphs; and
     Conclusions and recommendations.

TMC is required to submit all documents in electronic format to the State Water
Resources Control Board’s GeoTracker database, pursuant to the California Code of
Regulations (Title 23, Section 3890, et.seq.). Guidance for electronic information
submittal is available at
http://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/ust/electronic_submittal . Please
note that this requirement includes all analytical data, monitoring well information
(latitudes, longitudes, elevations, and water depth), site maps, and boring logs. All
reports submitted should have the Regional Water Board file number 01S0773 on the
first page of the report.
File No.: 01S0773                                                                Page 3 of 3


Basis for Reports Requests
The information requested is needed to reduce or eliminate future impacts to human
health or water quality from the subject Source Property’s contamination, to help
determine the stability of the groundwater plume, and to monitor the effectiveness of
secondary source area treatment. TMC is requested to provide the reports and
information requested in this letter in its capacity as the current owner and operator of
the subject Source Property.

Please direct all questions and correspondence regarding this matter to Mr. Ralph
Lambert via e-mail Ralph.Lambert@waterboards.ca.gov.

                                      CASE NARRATIVE

Laboratory number:                  305141
Clien t:                            Piers Environmental Services
Proje c t:                          1255 EASTSHORE
Location:                           1255 Eastshore
Request Date:                       11/16/18
Samples Received :                  11/16/18


This data package contains sample and QC results for fifteen soil samples ,
requested for the above referenced project on 11/16/18 . The samples were
received cold and intact .

TPH-Purgeables and/or BTXE by GC (EPA 8015B):
High recovery was observed for gasoline C7 - C12 in the MSD for batch 265538 ;
the parent sample was not a project sample , the BS/BSD were within limits ,
the associated RPO was within limits , and this analyte was not detected at or
above the RL in the associated samples . High surrogate recoveries were
observed for bromofluorobenzene (FID) in many samples . No other analytical
problems were encountered .

TPH-Extractables by GC (EPA 8015B) :
Matrix spikes QC956543 , QC956544 (batch 265704) were not analyzed because the
parent sample required a dilution that would have diluted out the spikes .
MW2D4 . l ' (lab # 305141 - 006) , MW4D4 . 2 ' (lab # 305141 - 012) , and MW2DRUM (lab #
305141 - 014) were diluted due to the dark and viscous nature of the sample
extracts. No other analytical problems were encountered .

Volatile Organics by GC/MS (EPA 8260B):
Matrix spikes were not performed for this analysis in batch 265569 due to
insufficient sample amount . Matrix spikes were not performed for this
analysis in batch 265574 due to insufficient sample amount. Low recovery was
observed for chlorobenzene in the MSD of MW2D8 (lab# 305141 - 007) ; the BS/BSD
were within limits , and the associated RPO was within limits . High surrogate
recovery was observed for bromofluorobenzene in MW2DRUM (lab# 305141 - 014) .
MW104 . 2 (lab# 305141 - 002) , MW3D6 . 5 ' (lab# 305141 - 010) , and MW4D9 ' (lab#
305141 - 013) were not diluted ; the low sample weight is due to 5035 packaging .
MW2D4 . 1 ' (lab# 305141 - 006) and MW2DRUM (lab# 305141 - 014) were diluted due
to high hydrocarbons . No other analytical problems were encountered .

                                   CASE NARRATIVE

Laboratory number:              294680
Clien t :                       Piers Environmental Services
Location:                       1255 Eastshore
Request Date :                  11/21/17
Samples Received:               11/21/17


This data package contains sample and QC results for fourteen soil samples
and six water samples, requested for the above referenced project on
11/21/17. The samples were received cold and intact.

TPH-Purgeables and/or BTXE by GC (EPA 8015B) Water :
Low responses were observed for gasoline C7 - C12 in the CCV analyzed 11/23/17
04:58, the CCV analyzed 11/23/17 12:48, and the CCV analyzed 11/23/17 18:50;
affected data was qualified with "b". High surrogate recoveries were observed
for bromofluorobenzene (FID) in B3 WATER (lab# 294680 - 017) and B4 WATER (lab
# 294680 - 018) . A number of samples had pH greater than 2. No other analytical
problems were encountered .

TPH-Purgeables and/or BTXE by GC (EPA 8015B) Soil :
High surrogate recoveries were observed for bromofluorobenzene (FID) in
B3D3.2 ' (lab# 294680 - 007), B3D5.2 ' (lab# 294680 - 008), and B4D5.2 (lab#
294680 - 010). No other analytical problems were encountered.

TPH-Extractables by GC (EPA 8015B) Water :
No analytical problems were encountered.

TPH-Extractables by GC (EPA 8015B) Soil :
Many samples were diluted due to the dark and viscous nature of the sample
extracts. No other analytical problems were encountered.

Volatile Organics by GC/MS (EPA 8260B) Wat er :

                                       CASE NARRATIVE

Laboratory number:                  300580
Clien t:                            Piers Environmental Services
Location:                           1255 Eastshore
Request Date :                      06/12/18
Samples Received:                   06/12/18


This data package contains sample and QC results for nine soil samples and
three water samples , requested for the above referenced project on 06/12/18 .
The samples were received cold and intact .

TPH-Purgeables and/or BTXE by GC (EPA 8015B) Water:
No analytical problems were encountered .

TPH-Purgeables and/or BTXE by GC (EPA 8015B) Soil:
No analytical problems were encountered .

TPH-Extractables by GC (EPA 8015B) Water :
No analytical problems were encountered .

TPH-Extractables by GC (EPA 8015B) Soil :
A number of samples were diluted due to the dark and viscous nature of the
sample extracts . No other analytical problems were encountered .

Volatile Organics by GC/MS (EPA 8260B) Water:
B9WATER (lab# 300580 - 011) was diluted due to high SO2 . B8WATER (lab#
300580 - 010) and Bl0WATER (lab# 300580 - 012) were diluted due to foaming .
Bl0WATER (lab# 300580 - 012) had pH greater than 2 . No other analytical
problems were encountered .

Volatile Organics by GC/MS (EPA 8260B) Soil :
High response was observed for 2 - butanone in the CCV analyzed 06/19/18 07 : 59 ;
affected data was qualified with " b ". Matrix spikes were not performed for
this analysis in batch 260568 due to insufficient sample amount . Response
exceeding the instrument ' s linear range was observed for acetone in B9O4 . 5 '
(lab # 300580 - 005) ; affected data was qualified with " b ". B8O9 . 7 ' (lab #
300580 - 003) , B9O10 ' (l ab # 300580 - 006) , and B10O6 . 7 ' (lab # 300580 - 009) were
not diluted ; the low sample weight is due to 5035 packaging . No other
analytical problems were encountered .

Metals (EPA 6010B) Soil :
No analytical problems were encountered .

Metals (EPA 6010B) Filtrate :
No analytical problems were encountered .

                                        CASE NARRATIVE

Laboratory number:                   300394
Clien t:                             Piers Environmental Services
Location:                            1255 Eastshore
Request Date :                       06/05/18
Samples Received:                    06/05/18


This data package contains sample and QC results for nineteen soil samples
and six water samples , requested for the above referenced project on
06/05/18. The samples were received cold and intact .

TPH-Purgeables and/or BTXE by GC (EPA 8015B) Water:
No analytical problems were encountered .

TPH-Purgeables and/or BTXE by GC (EPA 8015B) Soil:
High surrogate recoveries were observed for bromofluorobenzene (FID) in
B15D3 ' (lab # 300394 - 014) , B15D4 . 5 ' (l ab # 300394 - 015) , and B7D4 . 3 ' (l ab #
300394 - 018) . No other analytical problems were encountered .

TPH-Extractables by GC (EPA 8015B) Water:
No analytical problems were encountered .

TPH-Extractables by GC (EPA 8015B) Soil :
Many samples were diluted due to the dark and viscous nature of the sample
extracts . No other analytical problems were encountered .

Volatile Organics by GC/MS (EPA 8260B) Water :
B7 WATER (lab# 300394 - 020) was diluted due to high non - target analytes . A
number of samples were diluted due to foaming . No other analytical problems
were encountered.

Volatile Organics by GC/MS (EPA 8260B) Soil :
High recovery was observed for trichloroethene in the MSD for batch 260254 ;
the parent sample was not a project sample , the BS/BSD were within limits ,
the associated RPD was within limits , and this analyte was not detected at or
above the RL in the associated samples . Low recovery was observed for toluene
in the MSD for batch 260340 ; the parent sample was not a project sample , the
LCS was within limits , the associated RPD was within limits, and the low
recovery was not associated with any reported results . High recovery was
observed for trichloroethene in the MS for batch 260236 ; the parent sample
was not a project sample, the BS/BSD were within limits, the associated RPD
was within limits , and this analyte was not detected at or above the RL in
the associated sample . High surrogate recovery was observed for
bromofluorobenzene in B15D4.5 ' (lab# 300394 - 015) . Low surrogate recoveries
were observed for dibromofluoromethane in the MS/MSD for batch 260254 ; the
parent sample was not a project sample . A number of samples were diluted due
to high hydrocarbons . B12D4 . 7 ' (lab # 300394 - 005) and B7D9. 7 ' (lab #
300394 - 019) were not diluted ; the low sample weight is due to 5035 packaging .
No other analytical problems were encountered .

Southwick 1035 Eastshore Hwy LLC

Subject:      Approval of Report and Requirement for Groundwater Monitoring
              Investigation at 1255 Eastshore Highway, Berkeley, Alameda County

Dear Mr. Southwick:

This letter approves your April 12, 2019 Additional Investigations Completion Report.
This letter also requires Southwick 1035 Eastshore Hwy LLC to submit an Additional
Investigations Report.

Background
The Regional Water Board November 21, 2018 directive letter (Directive) required that
you submit a completion report documenting additional investigations conducted at the
subject Site to address identified data gaps by April 13, 2019. Hydrocarbon and volatile
organic compound (VOC) impacted soils were identified at the Site during trenching
activities associated with site improvements. Phase II investigations indicated that soils
and shallow groundwater contained concentrations of hydrocarbons and VOCs
exceeding the Tier 1 Environmental Screening Levels (ESLs). Required additional
investigations were completed to define the nature and extent of soil, soil vapor and
groundwater contamination; and evaluate potential indoor air impacts via the vapor
intrusion exposure pathway.

Report Summary
The completed investigation included the following:

   •   Sub-slab soil vapor sample collection at six locations;
   •   Four groundwater monitoring well installations;
   •   Soil sampling at various depths in monitoring well borings;
   •   Groundwater sampling from four new monitoring wells;
   •   Indoor Air sample collection at four locations and one outdoor air location to
       evaluate ambient air.

One soil sample contained petroleum–gasoline at a concentration exceeding ESLs, and
this sample was bounded vertically and horizontally by samples with petroleum-gasoline
concentrations below ESLs. The only constituents of concern (COCs) detected in

                           DR. TERRY F. YOUNG, Cf<AIR    I MICHAEL MONTGOMERY' EXECUTIVE OFFICER
                      1515 Clay St., Suite 1400, Oakland, CA 94612 I www.wa1erboards.ca.gov/sanlranclscobay
01S0790


groundwater at concentrations exceeding the drinking water Maximum Contaminant
Levels (MCLs) were cis-1,2 dichloroethylene and trichloroethylene. These compounds
were not detected in soil vapor samples. COCs detected in soil vapor at concentrations
exceeding the ESLs were ethylbenzene, vinyl chloride, and xylenes. None of the COCs
detected at concentrations exceeding ESLs in groundwater, soil or soil vapor were
detected in indoor air samples; and the outdoor air sample contained the same
compounds and COC concentrations as the indoor air samples.

Based on the data reported it appears that COCs identified in the subsurface are not
migrating to indoor air via vapor intrusion pathway. The lateral extent of VOC impacted
groundwater has not been adequately defined, therefore Regional Water Board staff
concurs with the Consultant’s recommendation to install two additional groundwater
monitoring wells.

Approval of Report
The Report satisfies the requirements of our November 2018 Directive letter. I approve
the Report.

Requirement for an Additional Investigation Report
Southwick 1035 Eastshore Hwy LLC is required to submit an Additional Investigation
Report by November 30, 2019. The Additional Investigation Report should provide
results of the additional groundwater monitoring proposed in the approved Report. The
Additional Investigation Report shall include the following element(s):
   • Installation details for two additional groundwater monitoring wells (including well
       locations, logs of borings and well completion diagrams).
   • Analytical data reports for groundwater sampling.
   • Updated conceptual site model showing the lateral extent of VOC impacted
       groundwater.
   • Proposed future groundwater monitoring plan to assess plume stability (including
       wells to be monitored, frequency and parameters to be analyzed).

Southwick 1035 Eastshore Hwy LLC is required to submit all documents in electronic
format to the State Water Resources Control Board’s GeoTracker database, pursuant to
the California Code of Regulations (Title 23, Section 3890, et.seq.). See Electronic
Submittal of Information for guidance on submitting documents to GeoTracker. Please
note that this requirement includes all analytical data, monitoring well information
(latitudes, longitudes, elevations, and water depth), site maps, and boring logs.

Basis for Requirement
The information required in this report is needed to define the extent of the groundwater
contamination plume and any immediate threats it poses to human health or water
quality.

Southwick 1035 Eastshore Hwy LLC is named in its capacity as the current landowner.

This requirement for a report is made pursuant to Water Code Section 13267, which
allows the Water Board to require technical or monitoring program reports from any
person who has discharged, discharges, proposes to discharge, or is suspected of

Hello Donal,

I reviewed your closure request report and lots of other reports in GT.. The Report requests case closure. I cannot
close the case at this me. I understand the site is located in an manufacturing and industrial part of Berkeley and
groundwater is encountered at less than 5 feet deep and is not used for drinking. However, we need to
demonstrate the site meets all the low-threat case closure criteria presented in the Water Board’s guidance
documents. Please provide addi onal informa on below:

    1. The report states that in three quarters of groundwater monitoring data, only TCE (detected at 82 µg/L in
       MW-1 in June 2019) exceeded the Final Aqua c Habitat ESL of 81 µg/L. Did the Water Board concur that
       the Aqua c Habitat ESL is the cleanup goal for groundwater?
    2. Groundwater has been sample four mes in 2019, but the data is not tabulated on a single table to show
       concentra on trends. Also concentra ons over me graphs are helpful to show trends and demonstrate
       plume stability, plume delinea on, decreasing concentra on trends, when concentra on exceed
       environmental screening levels. Groundwater is not delineated in the northwest and the only data point to
       the west is from a grab sample B14 that showed no VOCs. An oﬀsite source of VOCs coming onto the site
       from upgradient direc ons is ques onable without addi onal data.
    3.
    4. The former drum storage area in the NE corner of the property was not inves gated and it could contain
       residual sources of contamina on.
    5. The argument that PCE and TCE are from oﬀsite sources needs to be supported with addi onal data from
       upgradient of the site. I found two sites in Geotracker that may assist you in ge ng addi onal PCE and TCE
       data. Dove Chemical at 707 Park located at Harrison and Cedarwood is a possible source of VOCs but a File
       Review is needed since Geotracker has no info on it. Also, a LUFT site site at 707 Gilman (at Park) found PCE
       up to 28,000 ug/l.
    6. Two rounds in IA sampling were done, both events happened in the Fall. The elevated PCE and TCE in
       background samples from ambient sources is also not fully explained. Did you have evidence that workers
       were spraying those chemicals on the day you sampled? Did you take steps to remove all VOC sources
       before sampling IA?

    Please provide addi onal informa on on the drum storage area (DSA) located in the NW corner of the site,
    based on Figures presented in the Phase 1 ESA. The ﬁgures presented in PIERS Reports do not iden fy the
    DSA. Are you aware of it? Let me know if you want to do a conference call. Thanks.
